title: The House of Wisdom
objective: After this level you can explain how Baghdad became a center of learning.
summary: The Abbasids overthrew the Umayyads in 750; al-Mansur founded Baghdad as the Round City in 762. Al-Ma'mun sponsored Greek translation; the House of Wisdom's scope is debated.

cards.headline: In 762 a caliph built his capital as a circle. It became a city of translators.
cards.body: Under the caliph al-Ma’mun, Baghdad turned ancient Greek books into Arabic. At the heart of the story sits a famous name, the House of Wisdom. What was it, really?

cards.headline: A new family, a round city
cards.body: Remember Level 8’s Umayyad caliphs, ruling from Damascus? In 750 a new family, the Abbasids, overthrew them, and the capital later moved to a brand-new city. In 762 the caliph al-Mansur chose the site of Baghdad and built Madinat al-Salam, the City of Peace, inside circular walls. Everyone called it the Round City. Most capitals grow; this one was drawn.

cards.headline: Greek books, Arabic words
cards.body: The caliph al-Ma’mun, who reigned from 813 to 833, encouraged the translation of ancient Greek works into Arabic. From about 800 to 1000, a large-scale translation movement carried Aristotle, Euclid and much more into Arabic. Picture a whole library learning a new language, one book at a time.
cards.callout: About 800 to 1000: Greek learning moves into Arabic

cards.headline: The House of Wisdom puzzle
cards.body: Bayt al-Hikmah, the House of Wisdom, was a royal library of the Abbasid caliphs, and it reached its peak under al-Ma’mun. It is often pictured as a great academy at the centre of everything. Historians are more careful: little evidence puts it at the centre of Baghdad’s scholarship, so its scope is debated. The translating itself is not in doubt. The legend may be bigger than the building; the books were real.

mascot.line: A famous building that might have been mostly a bookshelf. History loves a plot twist.

questions.prompt: What did people call the Abbasid capital that al-Mansur founded at Baghdad in 762?

options.label: The White City
options.rationale: Its name came from its shape.

options.label: The City of Towers
options.rationale: Think of the shape of its walls.

questions.explanation: Al-Mansur’s Madinat al-Salam was built inside circular walls, so it was called the Round City.

questions.prompt: Why do historians debate what Baghdad’s House of Wisdom really was?

options.label: No translations were ever made in Baghdad
options.rationale: The translation movement was large and real.

options.label: It was a library in Damascus, not Baghdad
options.rationale: It was the Abbasid caliphs’ library in Baghdad.

options.label: Little evidence puts it at the centre of scholarship
Its books were written only in Greek
options.rationale: The movement put Greek works into Arabic.

questions.explanation: It was a royal library, but little evidence shows it was the centre of Baghdad’s scholarship, so its scope is debated.

questions.prompt: The Abbasids overthrew a dynasty in 750. Which one, whose capital Level 8 placed in Damascus?
questions.explanation: The Umayyad caliphs had moved the capital to Damascus; the Abbasids overthrew them in 750.
